t: This is the tomb of James Stephen, in the churchyard of the Old Church of St Mary in Hackney. Stephen is buried here. He was the principal English lawyer associated with the movement to abolish slavery. Born in Poole in Dorset, he later moved with his family to Stoke Newington. His descendants were remarkable too. His son was Sir James Stephen, and his grandsons were Sir James Fitzjames Stephen and Sir Leslie Stephen. Virginia Woolf and Vanessa Bell were his great-grandchildren. So a quiet churchyard tomb holds a link between the abolition campaign and one of Britain's best-known literary families.
